result.title: Not the Scalar, but Its Evolution: Robust Source Attribution for Generated Images
result.summary: The widespread deployment of latent generative models (LGMs) makes generated image source attribution essential for copyright auditing and data governance, yet practical attribution should remain reliable under common post-processing and platform-induced processing. Existing reconstruction-based attribution methods summarize an image's reconstruction response to a single global scalar, such as the reconstruction error or the ratio of two consecutive errors. These summaries discard channel-frequency structure, allowing image content and post-processing variation to obscure source evidence and making attribution after spreading difficult. We instead uncover a more stable source-discriminative cue under post-processing: the frequency-resolved evolution of residual energy across repeated applications of the same reconstruction operator. Motivated by this insight, we characterize a phenomenon we term Spectral Contraction and use it to build SpCon, a source-attribution framework that accesses only the target model's VAE. SpCon obtains adjacent residuals through two deterministic reconstructions, builds a spectral-contraction representation from their frequency-resolved relative energy change, and aggregates Student-t response densities for each source-condition pair over a finite set of fitted reference components. The same representation supports three settings according to non-belonging reference availability: none (Target-Only, TO; belonging references only), external out-of-domain sources (External-Reference, ER), or known in-domain competitors (Known-Reference, KR). Across seven LGMs, TO, ER, and KR attain average AUROC/AP of 0.8786/0.6344, 0.9404/0.7886, and 0.9652/0.8626 over the 35 conditions, all outperforming the strongest baseline (0.8154/0.5277), and achieve 0.8581/0.5507, 0.9369/0.7549, and 0.9734/0.8773 on the three social platforms.

AI.brief_summary: 论文面向生成图像的来源归因：指出以往方法把重建响应压成单一标量会丢失通道—频率结构，转而刻画同一重建算子重复作用时残差能量的频率分辨演化（称为 Spectral Contraction），并据此构建仅依赖目标模型 VAE 的 SpCon 框架，在多种参考条件与平台上评估归因性能。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「多次重建下频率分辨残差变化」可视为一种探查 VAE 潜表示中保留了哪些视觉细节的探针，或可供核查用于诊断 LVR 内部状态的信息坍缩与视觉证据保留；但论文本身不涉及推理过程。
